purpose: Check the long transcript for gross loss/repetition by comparing its book body to a separately prepared published text. This is agreement with book text, NOT measured full-file or validated speech-recognition accuracy.
independence: No benchmark scorer, runner, or transcription application was imported. jiwer/RapidFuzz performs optimized alignment; no quadratic Python CER matrix was used.

source.title: The Time Machine (Version 3), Chapter 5
source.book_body_reference_scope: Book body only. Does not include spoken recording title/introduction/outro; exact audio boundary offsets have not been manually established. Narration deviations have not been exhaustively manually audited. Do not report full-file WER against this body-only reference as ground truth without boundary/reference validation.
source.reference_extraction: Body prose of current Gutenberg sections VII (A Sudden Shock) and VIII (Explanation), concatenated in source order; source chapter headings removed and paragraph-internal whitespace collapsed. This corresponds to Chapter V in the older 12-chapter edition used for the recording. No ASR output was used to generate or correct this reference.

input_integrity.interpretation: The tested input is a lossless MP3-to-MKV remux, not the original MP3 container. Both compressed audio packet content and decoded PCM hashes are identical, while container hashes appropriately differ. The tested MKV hash matches before/after run metrics.

body_selection.method: First unique opening anchor through the complete segment containing the unique closing anchor. Anchors identify book body only; no manual audio boundary or narration-reference validation was performed.

body_selection.closing_anchor: and very soon she was smiling and clapping her hands while i solemnly

exploratory_published_book_text_agreemen.normalization: Unicode NFKC/casefold; letters, marks and numbers retained; punctuation/symbols become spaces; whitespace collapsed. No numeric-word, alternate-spelling or edition equivalence. Character ratio includes spaces.

gross_continuity_checks.finding: The alignment shows no paragraph-scale missing or repeated passages. The largest book-only span is 15 words, but its absence cannot be attributed to ASR without checking the narration/edition. This does not prove every spoken word was transcribed.

salient_differences.reference: even anger at the folly of leaving the machine having leaked away with my strength
salient_differences.interpretation: Secondary small-model recognition of the local audio excerpt also lacks this clause. Together with the short timestamp gap this supports a narration/edition difference, but is not human-audited proof. Do not count it as a confirmed ASR omission.

salient_differences.reference: eight hundred and two thousand seven hundred and one
salient_differences.interpretation: The raw text metric counts substitutions/deletions for number spelling versus digits; this is not a seven-word missing spoken passage.
Possible loss of the word Chapter in the primary output. Neither output establishes manually verified opening speech. No evidence here supports inventing an omitted long LibriVox introduction.
Some differences are orthographic or wording variants; others may be recognition errors. Classification is not exhaustive auditory adjudication.

ending_signal_check.method: Independent ffmpeg run on actual tested MKV: silencedetect=noise=-40dB:d=2; this is a signal-level threshold check, not human listening.
ending_signal_check.interpretation: The final output timestamp lies within the detected final silence. The approximately 10.95-second unrepresented tail is consistent with silence, not evidence of missing narration.
